alt: A word's characters are sliced three ways: word[1:4], word[:3] and word[3:]. On a full-length word all three slices hold characters; on a one-character word two of the three come out empty, showing that a slice never raises an error.

steps.caption: `word[1:4]` is "lep": everything from index 1 up to, but not including, index 4.
`word[:3]` is "ele": leaving out the start begins from index 0.
`word[3:]` is "phant": leaving out the stop runs to the end of the word.
`word[1:4]` is "": nothing is left starting from index 1, so the slice is empty.
`word[:3]` is "x": leaving out the start begins from index 0.
`word[3:]` is "": index 3 is already at or past the last character.
